extracted.intended_audience: researchers, developers, and graduate students working on computational humor, NLP, and joke-generation systems
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, evaluating, or producing computational systems that generate or analyze humor (puns, sarcasm, metaphor, etc.) using knowledge bases, conceptual blending, and related cognitive theories. Emphasis on both algorithmic generation and hybrid template-based approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a conceptual blend at the core?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a conceptual blend at the core?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A computational joke should center on a blend of two (or more) concepts whose features are recombined. The blend is the generative mechanism for the humorous meaning rather than a mere juxtaposition of unrelated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are two domains structure-mapped?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the system establishes systematic correspondences (structure-mapping/analogical links) between source and target domains. Success requires coherent mapping of roles and relations, not only superficial lexical overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the blend produce coherent surprise?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the blend produce coherent surprise?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor requires surprise that is also interpretable: the blend should yield an unexpected output that the audience can make sense of. Avoid blends that are merely chaotic or incoherent; the surprise must be explainable in terms of the mapped structure/features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the metaphor pushed into wit (not just description)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the metaphor pushed into wit (not just description)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphors should be exploited to create a twist or literalization that yields humor, rather than being used as plain descriptive language. The system should move beyond identifying a metaphor to manipulating or literalizing terms to produce an ironic or witty effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is wisdom (truth) present alongside wit?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective humor often pairs cleverness with an insight or recognizable truth. Judge whether the output conveys an observation or aphoristic 'wisdom' in addition to surface wit; mere wordplay without resonance is weaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge-base and resource coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of wide knowledge bases and relevant linguistic/commonsense resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Veale argues joke generation is knowledge-based: systems should have broad factual, lexical, and encyclopedic knowledge to support blending and to recognize targets. Check for coverage of world knowledge, lexical ambiguities, ontologies, and cultural facts that enable plays on meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms for blending concepts (algorithmic support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms for blending concepts (algorithmic/computational blending and mapping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond asserting a blend, a system must implement mechanisms (e.g., conceptual blending algorithms, structure-mapping procedures, metaphorical mapping heuristics) to create and evaluate blends. Assess whether the system contains explicit algorithms to identify candidate domains, align structure, and generate blended outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern templates and canned/joint approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of pre-scripted templates (canned jokes) versus algorithmic generation; preference for hybrids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some humor can be successfully produced from templates; others require algorithmic combination. Veale recommends hybrid systems. Evaluate whether the system appropriately integrates templates/patterns with generative blending to balance fluency and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of multiple humor types (puns, sarcasm, metaphor, metonymy, offensiveness modulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capability to generate/detect different humor types: puns (phonological/lexical ambiguity), sarcasm (meaning inversion), metaphor/metonymy, and to detect/modulate offensiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess support for specific phenomena: puns require phonological and lexical ambiguity handling; sarcasm needs contextual inversion detection and pragmatic cues; metaphors require mapping and literalization; systems should also include filters or modulation for offensiveness where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stereotype inversion pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of stereotype inversion as a humor pattern (reverse expectations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stereotype inversion—mapping expectations to reversed roles ('X is to Y what Z is to W' — reverse expectations)—is a productive pattern. Evaluate whether the system can identify stereotypes and invert them coherently to produce humorous contrast without resorting to incoherence or gratuitous offensiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metaphor-with-twist / literalization pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphor with twist: employ a standard metaphor and then literalize or twist one term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A common pattern is to take a familiar metaphor (e.g., 'love is war') and literalize one of the components to create an absurd or witty image. Judge whether the system can select apt metaphors and perform principled literalizations that yield humor rather than simply nonsensical outputs.
